summary: Intermittent model artifact fetch timeouts caused by AAAA responses and unreachable IPv6 path on private deployment
description: Issue summary: Customer reported intermittent failures pulling model artifacts and sporadic 504/504-like timeouts from the loader process on their private deployment. Impact: model loads fail ~1-3 times per hour for a subset of hosts, causing prediction errors and degraded streaming sessions. Environment: Private deployment, peered VPCs between Acero and Redwood control plane in us-east-1. Symptoms observed by customer: long stalls (~45-90s) before retries, then successful fallback. Relevant for long-lived chat sessions and initial model pulls after scale-up.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a private node behind Acero's peered VPC (us-east-1) using the provided helm chart
2) Trigger a model pull by starting multiple worker containers concurrently (10+), or initiate a cold-start streaming session
3) Observe loader logs for connect/connect timeout errors and an eventual fallback to IPv4 after a long delay
4) Capture DNS responses for control plane and artifact S3 endpoints during the failure window
logs: Mar 07 12:14:03 loader[pid]: pulling artifact from artifacts.redwood.example.com -> resolved to [2604:abc0:...]:443, fallback to 3.212.45.12 after timeout
Mar 07 12:14:49 http client: connect timeout to 2604:abc0:...:443 (connect(2) timed out), retrying via A record
Mar 07 12:14:52 loader[pid]: artifact fetch successful via 3.212.45.12 after 49s
tcpdump snippet from customer: SYN to IPv6 address, no SYN-ACK observed; following SYN to IPv4 succeeds
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: intermittent firewall/NAT blocking or asymmetric routing causing stream resets

Observed pattern: DNS answers sometimes include AAAA for artifacts/control-plane hostnames returned by Acero's split-DNS resolver for certain AZs. When AAAA is returned, hosts attempt IPv6 connections which hang (no SYN-ACK) for long TCP connect timeout before resolver/client falls back to IPv4.

Redwood SRE ran parallel tests from a repro host in customer environment: consistent AAAA responses from 169.254.169.x-based DNS forwarder in specific subnets, but IPv6 path does not exist beyond the NGFW (customer confirmed ICMPv6 and IPv6 routing disabled on corporate egress).

Key finding: Customer split-horizon DNS accidentally published IPv6 (AAAA) records for public artifact/control-plane names in some private zones. Their egress path does not support IPv6, so attempts stall until client fallback, causing service-visible timeouts. This only impacts short-lived connections or cold-starts where the single connection attempt is blocked long enough to trigger user-visible errors.
Relevant telemetry: increased connect_time and socket_connect_time metrics from serving-runtime correlating with DNS AAAA answers; no application-layer 5xx from Redwood backend.

Corroborating evidence: tcpdump and traceroute to AAAA address show packets leaving host but being dropped at customer NGFW (confirmed by customer firewall logs showing no IPv6 route and dropped traffic).

2026-03-07 16:45 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Verified pcap. Confirmed SYN->AAAA with no SYN-ACK. Firewall team says IPv6 routing is not enabled outbound; split-DNS zone apparently contains stale AAAA entries from an older internal record set.

2026-03-08 09:12 - Acero (Network team): We removed AAAA records from the private zone for the artifacts and control plane hostnames. We will also add a short-term fix to the nodes to prefer IPv4 by adjusting /etc/gai.conf. Request: any recommendation on short-term kernel tweaks for our hosts to avoid fallback delays?

2026-03-08 10:01 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Recommend adding 'precedence ::ffff:0:0/96  100' to /etc/gai.conf to prefer IPv4 for dual-stack lookups, and lowering TCP connect timeout for our loader to shorten fallback window as an additional mitigation. We'll also add detection rule to Console to flag when AAAA is returned but IPv6 handshakes fail.
2026-03-10 11:27 - Acero (Customer): After removing AAAA records and applying gai.conf change our error rate dropped to baseline. No further timeouts observed.
resolution_notes: Root cause: split-DNS for Acero's private zone contained stale AAAA records for Redwood artifact/control-plane hostnames. Customer egress path lacked IPv6 routing/egress; IPv6 connect attempts stalled until client fallback to IPv4, producing user-visible timeouts.

Action taken: Customer removed AAAA records from private DNS and applied an /etc/gai.conf preference for IPv4 as a short-term host-side mitigation. Redwood updated loader docs to call out recommendation for dual-stack environments to prefer IPv4 when IPv6 egress is not guaranteed.

Follow-ups: (1) Added a Console alert rule to flag high socket_connect_time correlated with AAAA answers. (2) Engineering task created to make loader TCP connect timeout configurable and to add faster parallel A/AAAA probing with early fallback — tracked in internal ticket INT-42902. (3) Customer agreed to add DNS hygiene check to their internal zone management to prevent publication of unused AAAA records.
Status: Resolved — monitoring shows no recurrence for 72+ hours in prod.
Customer impact: intermittent model pull failures resolved; no data loss.
